$comment: Analytics taxonomy — install family. Merged with its siblings by server/analytics.taxonomy(); see _envelope.json.

app_first_run.question: How many real installs are there?

app_launch_started.question: Do launches start, and did the previous one end cleanly?

backend_ready.question: How long until the API is usable?

launch_failure.question: Why can a user not get in at all?

session_started.question: The session denominator for every per-session rate.

session_ended.$comment: ENRICHMENT ONLY, never a denominator — a hard crash reaches neither before-quit nor pagehide.
session_ended.question: What shape does a session have?

provision_started.question: What blocks entry to the app on a first run?

provision_finished.$comment: Hooked at the AWAITED per-tier resolutions, NOT the NDJSON relay: the relay's first branch fires per LOG LINE (banned hook class 3). 1-2 per install.
provision_finished.question: Can a new user finish setup?

provisioning_error.$comment: SENS — the failure is CLASSIFIED locally; the raw stderr tail stays in the setup window and the local log, exactly as launch_failure already does.
provisioning_error.question: What is the first-run failure taxonomy?

provisioning_snapshot.$comment: CHANGE-ONLY against a module-level last-hash. /api/doctor is called by setup and Settings, not polled. free_gb and proxy_cache_mb are NOT in provision.doctor() — they are computed in the app-layer handler, which is also the only layer allowed to touch analytics.
provisioning_snapshot.question: What state are real installs actually in?

pack_install_outcome.$comment: Hooked at the SERVER streaming boundary. An earlier draft cited lib/provision.py, which is both a function DEFINITION and inside lib/ — violating the catalog's own banned-hook rule ('lib must not depend on server').
pack_install_outcome.question: Does anyone take the 2.6 GB pack?

update_lifecycle.question: Do users actually get our fixes?

open_vocabularies.target_version: A semver string from OUR published update feed. No user-input path.
